title: The trig six: per-surface sweeps with 460 held-out rows each, plus one group replay
upstream_status_verbatim: Validated `5425/5425` live rows (all six functions, incl. held-out sweeps and a bit-resolution COS threshold ladder).
status_plain: All six surfaces were scored individually -- the source's word is "each" -- so COT, CSC and SEC are measured surfaces, not inherited ones, even though only three kernels exist and the three reciprocals are built from the published primaries. 460 of each surface's 1020 (1044 for COS) rows were held out. The 5425/5425 in the same block is a different subject: a production-kernel replay over the deduplicated union, and it is a group total.

counts.build_note: The document header at line 9 names live Excel 16.0 build 20131, x86-64; the Sign-off block does not restate it. Not inherited.
counts.ambiguity_note: The source calls these figures "per-function unique survivors ... validation sweeps" -- the surviving candidate graph -- and reserves "production-kernel replay" for the group 5425/5425. The surviving candidate is what landed (mod.rs:426-427 attaches 1020/1020 to the production `excel_sin`), so the practical difference is nil, but the subject recorded here is the candidate score, which is the weaker reading.

evidence_locality_note: The W109 trig identification corpora live under `smart-fuzzer/work/` and `smart-fuzzer/cache/`, which are gitignored in OxFunc.
substrate: the legacy CRT fFSIN/fFPTAN chain with FPREM1 argument reduction against the 64-bit ROM pi; COT/CSC/SEC are `excel_x87_recip` of the published primaries
ruled_out: Cody-Waite reduction against extended pi -- the pre-sign-off catalogue row recorded moderate-large argument-reduction drift up to ~3.3E12 ULP
reader_warning: The catalogue restates only the group figure ("Validated 5425/5425 live rows (all six functions)"). Read alone that sentence gives no per-surface number and invites reading a group total as a per-surface rate. The per-surface figures live in the identification note, not the catalogue. All six inherit the host-CPU microcode caveat on FPREM1/FSIN/FPTAN.
